messages:
emily_support: FYI incoming escalation from a customer — embeddings vectors/sec dropped ~6x since last night, tokens/sec steady. They say requests either time out or return dimension_mismatch errors. Raising here for triage.

raj_ml: ugh, ok. do we have the customer id / example request?

emily_support: forwarded their snippet: `POST /v1/embeddings` payload: {\n  \"model\": \"redwood-embed-1\",\n  \"input\": [\"a short sentence\"]\}\nThey show response: `400 { \"error\": \"dimension_mismatch: expected dim=1536 got dim=1535\" }` sometimes 504s too.

mia_sre: @raj_ml possible batching/packing change in last deploy? Also check GPU queue_depth and kvcache backpressure.

raj_ml: pulling recent deploys... looks like autosplit batching tweak rolled out to hosted yesterday at 02:12 UTC. It lowered max_batch_size and enabled a new per-customer batching heuristic. Could be related.

alex_infra: checking infra metrics now. Prometheus snippet: `redwood_vecs_processed_total{model=\"redwood-embed-1\"} 1.2e6` but `vecs_per_sec` dropped from ~4800 -> ~800 at ~2026-02-25T02:30Z. GPU_util on cluster-gpu-4 is 95% but queue_depth has spiked: `inference_queue_depth{pool=\"embed-hosted\"} 182`.

emily_support: customer reported spike started around 02:27 UTC. They also mentioned intermittent 403s earlier but cleared after retry — might have been auth throttling?

mia_sre: 403s could be quota enforcement kicking in if backlog triggers an API-level limiter. But the dimension_mismatch errors are worrying — typically that means a model variant mismatch or post-quantization reshape bug. Any model rollouts?

raj_ml: we did roll a quantized variant to save cost for small-batch workloads three hours before. Could be an incompatible kernel for certain sequence lengths producing off-by-one dims on embeddings.

alex_infra: grab logs from host node 10.4.12.7: found repeated stack trace: ```
ERROR inference: encode: unexpected output size: expected 1536 got 1535
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/srv/runtime/encoder.py\", line 412, in forward
    out = quant_kernel.run(inp)
```
Looks correlated to our quant kernel version v1.3.2 that was in the rollout.

mia_sre: ok that explains dim mismatch. But why throughput drop? If many requests hitting nodes with kernel bug, they might error and not be retried or cause worker stalls. Check worker restart rates and backlog.

alex_infra: worker restarts spiked: `worker_restarts_total{node=\"10.4.12.7\"} +14` between 02:25-02:35. Also observed slow GC pauses in runtime logs, probably due to repeated error handling.

raj_ml: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) rollback quant kernel v1.3.2 on embed-hosted pool, 2) route traffic for redwood-embed-1 to fallback variant redwood-embed-1-stable, 3) increase per-instance concurrency to drain queue. Any objections?

emily_support: customer asked for ETA — can we do a quick rollback now?

alex_infra: rolling back kernel on 3/5 affected nodes now. deploy-bot: started rollback job id=rb-20260225-77.

deploy-bot: Rollback started for kernel v1.3.2 -> v1.3.1 on pool embed-hosted. Task rb-20260225-77 in progress.

mia_sre: while rollback runs, let's capture repro steps and a minimal request that triggers dim mismatch so we can write a regression test. emily, can you ask customer for the exact vector length they observed? Also request they include raw base64 response if available.

emily_support: asked — customer replied: they sent 1536-dim embeddings normally; the returned error said 1535. They also attached a curl they used: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":["test"]}'
```
They also tried `?batch_size=1` and saw the same.

raj_ml: interesting — batch_size=1 still fails implies not a batch packing bug but kernel-level assembly bug. I'll try to reproduce locally with the quant kernel. Repro steps I will run: 
1) checkout kernel v1.3.2
2) run unit tests with seq_len=1..64 and embedding dims 1536
3) run stress with 200 concurrent requests to simulate queue pressure

mia_sre: also check whether autoscaler reduced instance count earlier due to faulty health checks; that could cause GPU saturation and queue build. `autoscaler_desired_replicas{pool=\"embed-hosted\"}` dropped from 12 -> 4 at 02:20.

alex_infra: autoscaler logs show a misconfigured liveness probe change in the same deploy — caused premature scale-down. So two hits: faulty kernel + aggressive scale-down -> saturation -> queue_depth -> timeouts.

emily_support: customer still impacted but appreciates the quick responses. Any ETA on rollback completion?

deploy-bot: Rollback tasks completed on 4/5 nodes; final node draining now.

alex_infra: last node back to v1.3.1 and worker restarts halted. vecs_per_sec trending back up: 1200 -> 4200 over 5m. queue_depth decreasing.

raj_ml: I'll run the reproduction with v1.3.2 in a sandbox to capture exact failing input and add a unit/regression test. Also will add an integration test that validates embedding dimension == model.expected_dim in CI.

mia_sre: followups: 1) add a canary check for embedding output dims in rollout jobs, 2) tighten autoscaler hysteresis for embed pools, 3) add alert for sudden vecs_per_sec delta > 50% in 5m for hosted tier.

emily_support: sent a brief update to customer: rollback in progress, routing to stable variant, monitoring. They asked for root cause when done.

raj_ml: root cause summary draft: quant kernel v1.3.2 had an off-by-one in an assembly path for certain seq_len/alignments; combined with an autoscaler liveness probe change that allowed scale-down during the rollout, causing GPU saturation and higher error/restart rates. Fix: revert kernel & liveness probe change; add regression tests and canary checks; improve autoscaler hysteresis.

mia_sre: tagging ops runbook and postmortem owners: raj_ml (lead), alex_infra (infra follow-up), emily_support (customer comms). I'll open a postmortem thread once RCA confirmed.

emily_support: closing loop with customer now. Thanks everyone :heart:
